summary: This benchmark evaluates cross-model activation surgery by mapping a 7-dimensional activation subspace from a donor model (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B) to a host model (Qwen2.5-14B) via an affine transformation fitted with ridge regression. On a dataset of 497 initially solved Python operand evaluation pairs, the single-pass intervention achieved a 490/497 (98.59%) success rate, matching two-pass paired-donor differences and full host exchanges while orthogonal random controls achieved zero.
strengths: Rigorous experimental controls, including equal-norm orthogonal random controls, paired-donor difference arm, and full host state exchange baselines.

Precise reproducibility documentation, providing exact model revisions, layer cutoffs (donor block 6 to host block 10), subspace dimension (7), ridge regularization penalty (0.02), and software environment versions.
Dual-metric evaluation reporting both strict full-vocabulary argmax success and binary two-choice logit margins, backed by paired 95% confidence intervals.
weaknesses: Narrow benchmark domain focused solely on single-digit numeric arithmetic in short synthetic Python functions.
Lacks exploration across intermediate layers or varying subspace dimensions to demonstrate sensitivity to hyperparameter choices.
Submission is structured as a brief technical note (561 words) rather than a comprehensive benchmark report with broader behavioral evaluation.
suggestions: Extend the benchmark suite beyond single-digit Python arithmetic to multi-token reasoning or non-numeric variable substitution tasks.
Provide an ablation study examining how varying subspace dimensionality (e.g., d=1 to d=32) and different donor/host layer pairings affect transfer fidelity.
Officially bind the repository to the submission metadata rather than relying solely on embedded Markdown links.

claims.text: Use frozen Qwen2.5-Coder-7B base at revision `0396a76181e127dfc13e5c5ec48a8cee09938b02` and frozen Qwen2.5-14B base at revision `97e1e76335b7017d8f67c08a19d103c0504298c9`.
The one-pass advantage above random was +98.59 percentage points with a paired 95% interval of +97.38 to +99.60.
claims.source: Statistical binomial/score interval derivation based on 490/497 vs 0/497 paired outcomes

claims.text: The Studio run took 118 seconds under Python 3.12, MLX 0.32.4, MLX-LM 0.32.2 and NumPy 2.5.5.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Cross-Model Activation Stitching and Representation Universality
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Demonstrates that a low-dimensional (7D) affine subspace transformation without subtracting shared context achieves comparable steering fidelity to paired-difference and full-state exchanges on frozen model pairs.
